name: WinRAR
summary: WinRAR runs through Wine (trial nag included); Lindos also opens RAR archives natively.
notes:
WinRAR (32- and 64-bit installers) installs and runs through Wine: browsing, creating RAR/ZIP archives, extracting, repairing, password-protected and multi-volume archives, self-extracting (SFX) modules. The 40-day trial reminder appears exactly as on Windows; a licence key file (rarreg.key) dropped into the program folder registers it. Not available: the Windows Explorer context-menu integration and shell icons - use the Start Menu entry Lindos creates, or 'Open With > WinRAR' in the file manager.
You may not need it: Lindos extracts .rar files natively (right-click > Extract Here, using unrar/unar) and creates 7z/zip archives. WinRAR through Wine is mainly useful when you need to *create* RAR archives with the official tool.
This recipe creates a 64-bit C:\ drive with no special tweaks. Use the English 64-bit installer (winrar-x64-NNN.exe).

alternatives.name: Archive Manager (native)
alternatives.how: already installed on Lindos: right-click a .rar > Extract Here (apt install unrar for full RAR5 support)

alternatives.name: rar for Linux
alternatives.how: official command-line RARLAB build (creates RAR archives): apt install rar
